claims.text: Introducing a coherent, ordered L12-precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high-entropy alloy could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance.
The material initial state is Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Low-temperature annealing is the processing condition for the proposed improvement.
Low-temperature annealing precipitates ordered L12 intermetallic particles within the fcc phase.
The relevant structural mediator is a lamellar dual-phase fcc + B2 microstructure.
The L12 precipitates strengthen the alloy through Orowan dislocation bowing and bypass.
The intervention will enhance both strength and ductility relative to untreated high-entropy alloys.
The proposed effect should hold after low-temperature annealing under quasi-static or dynamic loading.
The effect of the intervention on strain-rate sensitivity is not fully understood.
Testing the alloy at different loading conditions and temperatures could be used to assess the prediction.

contradictions.description: The initial state is already Al0.7CoCrFeNi, while the intervention is described as introducing that same precipitation-strengthenable eutectic alloy rather than applying a distinct treatment such as low-temperature annealing.

The stated mediator is the pre-existing lamellar fcc + B2 structure, but the stated Orowan mechanism is attributed by the evidence to fine L12 precipitates; L12 precipitation is not identified as the structural mediator.
